Portimão is a Portuguese city in the District of Faro, in the Algarve region and sub-region, with about 40,000 inhabitants. The city centre is located about 2 km from the sea and is an important centre for fishing and tourism.

It is the seat of a municipality with an area of 182.06 km² and 55,614 inhabitants, subdivided into 3 parishes. The municipality is bordered to the north by the municipality of Monchique, to the east by Silves and Lagoa, and to the west by Lagos; to the south, it has a coastline on the Atlantic Ocean.

It has become a popular holiday destination, mainly due to the famous Praia da Rocha, and is also considered a city with great potential for enthusiasts of big fishing (e.g., swordfish), among other water sports such as jet skiing, sailing, windsurfing, diving, and spearfishing.
